name: OMM Decision-Sequence Pattern Explorer
jtbd: Hire this when a user has coded a decision process as ordered observations and wants to compare explicit HMM hypotheses, inspect step-level state probabilities, or explore fitting model parameters from multiple sequences.
runtime: Python >=3.11; pomegranate 1.1.2 (MIT) via optional hmm extra; local CLI, loopback web API, and stdio MCP tool
requires: at least two fully specified HMM parameter sets
limitations: The input research package does not provide numeric emissions or an initial state distribution; no default OMM model is shipped.
Relative model fit depends on caller-supplied feature coding and parameters and is not a validated measure of integrative thinking, ability, personality, or decision quality.
The capability compares models and returns posterior state probabilities; it does not generate opportunities or recommend a decision.
Exploratory Baum-Welch fitting is available only from explicit seed parameters and multiple coded sequences; the software minimum is not a statistical sufficiency claim.
The library returns posterior-MAP state labels by step, not a global Viterbi path.
MindrianOS must enforce authorization and retain any result in its own room or portfolio systems.
source_revision: independent standard HMM inference based on user-provided OM-HMM specification; no source code copied
license_status: independent implementation; source document provenance remains user-provided
